lessons.title: Greetings and simple replies
lessons.objective: Greet people, ask how they are, and give a natural short reply.

vocabulary.detail: A warm, very common greeting.
A polite greeting used in everyday life.
The usual reply to السلام عليكم.
A common Emirati/Gulf way to ask a man how he is.
The feminine form; pronunciation varies by speaker.
Can describe how you feel or how something is.

vocabulary.meaning: Thank God / praise be to God
vocabulary.detail: A common response after saying how you are.
A natural short positive reply.
Often used conversationally for emphasis, not always literally.
Informal singular “you”; feminine often إنتي.

structure.explanation: In a simple greeting exchange, speakers often use a greeting, ask how the other person is, then answer briefly. A full English-style sentence is not always needed.
structure.exampleEn: Hi, how are you? Fine, thank God.

notes.title: Greeting
notes.detail: Use هلا with friends and in casual situations; السلام عليكم works broadly.

notes.title: Replying
notes.detail: A short answer is natural. You can then ask و إنت؟ (“and you?”).

notes.title: Gender
notes.detail: The form can change depending on whether you address a man or a woman. Spellings and pronunciations vary across Emirati speakers.

exercises.question: What does زين mean in this context?
exercises.feedback: زين means good or fine.

exercises.question: Choose a natural reply to شحالك؟
exercises.feedback: زين، الحمد لله is a natural response: “Fine, thank God.”

lessons.title: What, where, and who
lessons.objective: Ask basic questions about people, places, and things.

vocabulary.detail: One of the most useful Emirati question words.
Used to ask about location.
Commonly used to ask who someone is.
Points to a masculine noun or something treated as masculine.
Points to a feminine noun or thing.
A complete, reusable question pattern.
Common Emirati/Gulf form meaning here.
A common word for there; local alternatives also occur.
A common noun for home or house.
Everyday word for a phone.

structure.explanation: Question words often come first. A simple location question can be “وين + thing/person?” A naming question can be “شو هذا؟” (“What is this?”) or “منو هذا؟” (“Who is this?”).

notes.title: Question word first
notes.detail: وين asks for a place; the place/person being asked about follows it.

notes.title: Demonstratives
notes.detail: Learn the noun together with the demonstrative when possible. Gender agreement is common, but everyday speech has variation.

notes.title: Short answers
notes.detail: A single location word can be a complete answer in conversation.

exercises.question: Which word asks “where”?
exercises.feedback: وين means where.

exercises.question: Complete the question: ___ هذا؟ (What is this?)
exercises.feedback: شو هذا؟ means “What is this?”

lessons.title: Wants and everyday needs
lessons.objective: Say what you want, need, have, or do not have.

vocabulary.detail: Very common Emirati way to say “I want”.
A useful verb for needs; أبغي can also be used for polite requests.

structure.explanation: A common request pattern is “أبغي + thing” (I want + thing). To say you have something, use “عندي + thing”; to say you do not have it, add ما before عندي.

notes.title: Wanting
notes.detail: أبغي ماي = I want water. The noun comes after أبغي.

notes.title: Possession
notes.detail: عندي سؤال = I have a question. ما عندي وقت = I don’t have time.

notes.title: Politeness
notes.detail: Add this before a request to soften it. Use an appropriate form for the person you address.

exercises.question: What does أبغي mean?
exercises.feedback: أبغي is the common Emirati “I want”.

exercises.question: How do you say “I don’t have time”?
exercises.feedback: ما عندي وقت = I don’t have time.

lessons.title: Today, yesterday, and later
lessons.objective: Talk about time and simple plans.

vocabulary.detail: Use it to anchor an action to today.
Common word for yesterday.
A characteristic Gulf/Emirati word for tomorrow.
Meaning depends on context; can mean afterwards.
Very common Emirati/Gulf time word.
Useful for delaying or sequencing an action.

A common time phrase.

structure.explanation: Time words can go at the beginning or end of a sentence. In colloquial speech, a b- prefix on a verb can signal an intended or future action, as in بروح (“I’ll go / I’m going”).

notes.title: Time first
notes.detail: Starting with اليوم makes the time frame clear.

notes.title: Future/intention
notes.detail: Forms such as بروح and بشوفك are common in everyday Gulf speech. Learn them as whole useful forms first.

notes.title: Sequencing
notes.detail: Use these to explain when something happens relative to another event.

exercises.question: Which word means “tomorrow” in Emirati Arabic?
exercises.feedback: باچر means tomorrow.

exercises.question: What does الحين mean?
exercises.feedback: الحين means now.

lessons.title: Family and friends
lessons.objective: Talk about family members and people close to you.

vocabulary.detail: Often used in expressions about family or household.
أم means mother; ـي means my.

structure.explanation: Possessive endings are very useful. For example, ـي often means “my”: أمي (my mother), أخوي (my brother), and أختي (my sister). Learn these common family words as complete forms.

notes.title: My + family member
notes.detail: The ending ـي means “my” in many nouns.

notes.title: With someone

notes.title: Asking about family
notes.detail: A friendly way to ask how someone’s family is doing; wording varies by speaker.

exercises.question: What does أخوي mean?
exercises.feedback: أخوي means my brother.

exercises.question: Which ending often means “my”?
exercises.feedback: The suffix ـي often means “my”.

lessons.title: At home and daily routines
lessons.objective: Describe home, daily activities, and routines.

vocabulary.detail: A room in a house or building.
The place where food is prepared.
Common household word.
An imperative commonly used for instructions.
Common spoken command.
First-person form in a simple present statement.
Colloquial everyday verb.

vocabulary.detail: Used in time expressions.
Marks a regular routine.
Useful for housework and organizing things.

structure.explanation: Daily routines are often described with a simple verb and an optional time phrase. Commands such as افتح and سكر are direct; add لو سمحت to make a request softer.

notes.title: Routine
notes.detail: أصحى الصبح = I wake up in the morning.

notes.title: Possession

notes.title: Commands
notes.detail: These are direct commands. For a polite request, use لو سمحت before or after the command.

exercises.question: What does كل يوم mean?
exercises.feedback: كل يوم means every day.

exercises.question: Which is a direct command meaning “open”?

lessons.title: Shopping and prices

Used for a low price.

Common borrowed word.

structure.explanation: To ask a price, say بكم هذا؟ (“How much is this?”). To describe the price, use غالي (expensive) or رخيص (cheap). وايد can mean “very / a lot” before an adjective.

notes.title: Price question
notes.detail: بكم هذا؟ = How much is this?

notes.title: Intensifier
notes.detail: وايد غالي = very expensive. In other contexts وايد can mean a lot/many.

notes.title: Payment
notes.detail: أدفع بالبطاقة = I pay by card. The ب in بالبطاقة means “by/with” here.

exercises.question: What does بكم؟ ask?
exercises.feedback: بكم؟ is used to ask a price.

exercises.question: وايد غالي means…
exercises.feedback: وايد means very/a lot, and غالي means expensive.

lessons.title: When you don’t understand
lessons.objective: Ask people to repeat, slow down, or explain.

vocabulary.detail: A useful phrase when you missed something.
A direct instruction; soften it when speaking politely.
Used to request repetition.
Common way to ask someone to slow down.
A useful word for making polite requests.
Used to ask someone to explain something.

Used to ask about a method or manner.
Useful for asking how to say a word.
Used to describe whether something is understandable.

structure.explanation: A polite request can be built with ممكن + verb (“Could you…?”). For example, ممكن تعيد؟ (“Could you repeat?”). You can explain the problem first with ما فهمت.

notes.detail: ممكن تعيد؟ = Could you repeat?

notes.title: Negative past meaning
notes.detail: This means “I didn’t understand.” Learn it as a complete phrase.

notes.title: Asking meaning
notes.detail: شو يعني؟ asks “What does it mean?” You can add the word or phrase after يعني.

exercises.question: What does ما فهمت mean?
exercises.feedback: ما فهمت means “I didn’t understand.”

exercises.question: How do you politely ask someone to repeat?
exercises.feedback: ممكن تعيد؟ means “Could you repeat?”

lessons.title: At work
lessons.objective: Talk about shifts, tasks, coworkers, and workplace needs.

vocabulary.detail: Meaning depends on context; often refers to being at work or a shift.
Broad everyday word for work or a job task.
vocabulary.exampleEn: I have a lot of work.

vocabulary.detail: A workplace role.

A coworker.
Common verb for arriving.
Useful for reporting a completed task.

Used for a person, task, or item that is ready.
Common administrative/workplace word.

structure.explanation: At work, شغل often means work or tasks, while دوام often means your workday, shift, or attendance at work. A short status update can be “خلصت الشغل” (“I finished the work”).

notes.title: Work nouns
notes.detail: شغل is the work/task itself; دوام often refers to working hours or a shift.

notes.title: Completed task
notes.detail: خلصت الشغل = I finished the work.

notes.title: Not yet
notes.detail: ما خلصت بعد = I haven’t finished yet. Learn this common pattern as a unit.

exercises.question: Which word often means work shift / working hours?
exercises.feedback: دوام often means work, a shift, or working hours.

exercises.question: ما خلصت بعد means…
exercises.feedback: ما خلصت بعد means “I haven’t finished yet.”

lessons.title: Asking for help and making requests
lessons.objective: Make practical requests and offer help politely.

vocabulary.detail: A direct request to one person.
A noun used with أحتاج (“I need”).
Polite, practical request.
Often used to ask whether someone can do something.
Introduces a condition.
A polite Gulf expression; literal wording is not the intended meaning.

notes.detail: ممكن تساعدني؟ = Could you help me?

notes.title: Can you…?
notes.detail: تقدر تساعدني؟ = Can you help me?

notes.title: Offering help
notes.detail: أقدر أساعدك = I can help you.

exercises.question: Which phrase means “Could you help me?”
exercises.feedback: ممكن تساعدني؟ is a polite request for help.

exercises.question: أقدر أساعدك means…
exercises.feedback: أقدر = I can; أساعدك = help you.

lessons.title: Making plans
lessons.objective: Suggest meeting, arrange a time, and confirm plans.

Question word for time.

Positive confirmation.

notes.detail: خلنا نروح = Let’s go.

notes.title: Plan question
notes.detail: متى نتلاقى؟ = When shall we meet?

exercises.question: Which word means “maybe”?
exercises.feedback: يمكن means maybe/perhaps.

lessons.title: Food, cafés, and preferences
lessons.objective: Order food and drinks and express what you like.

notes.title: Requesting the bill

exercises.question: ما أحب الحار means…

lessons.title: Explaining reasons and consequences
lessons.objective: Connect a reason to a result in a natural way.

vocabulary.detail: Introduces a reason.
vocabulary.exampleEn: I was late because the traffic was heavy.

vocabulary.detail: Very common colloquial connector; exact meaning depends on context.
A common Gulf connector for a consequence.

vocabulary.detail: Often used for traffic congestion.
Can intensify traffic, wind, taste, etc.
Masculine form; feminine is often تعبانة.
Another widely understood way to connect cause and result.
vocabulary.exampleAr: ما نمت زين، عشان كذا تعبان
vocabulary.exampleTrans: Mā nimt zain, ʿashān kitha taʿbān
vocabulary.exampleEn: I didn’t sleep well, that’s why I’m tired.

vocabulary.detail: A more formal word for result.

vocabulary.exampleEn: I was late because of the traffic.

vocabulary.detail: Introduces a purpose.

structure.pattern: Statement + because / that’s why + reason or result
structure.explanation: Use لأن or عشان to give a reason, and عشان جي / عشان كذا to introduce a result (“that’s why”). Choose the connector based on the relationship between the two ideas.
structure.exampleEn: I was late because traffic was heavy.

notes.title: Reason
notes.detail: تأخرت لأن الزحمة قوية = I was late because traffic was heavy.

notes.title: Consequence
notes.detail: كنت تعبان، عشان جي نمت = I was tired, that’s why I slept.

notes.title: Purpose
notes.detail: جيت عشان أشوفك = I came to see you / in order to see you.

exercises.question: Which expression means “that’s why”?
exercises.feedback: عشان جي commonly introduces a consequence: “that’s why”.

exercises.question: لأن usually introduces…
exercises.feedback: لأن means because and introduces a reason.

lessons.title: The word يعني in natural conversation

notes.title: Clarifying yourself

notes.title: Adding an example
notes.detail: مثلاً introduces a concrete example to make your meaning clearer.

exercises.question: In conversation, يعني can mean…
exercises.feedback: يعني has several conversational uses depending on context.

exercises.question: قصدي is useful when you want to…
exercises.feedback: قصدي means “I mean / what I mean is”.

lessons.title: Talking about a story or situation

exercises.question: Which phrase signals the end of a story?

lessons.title: Agreeing, disagreeing, and saying “it depends”

lessons.title: Clarifying a misunderstanding

lessons.title: Explaining what you’ve just done

vocabulary.detail: Common informal instruction to contact the speaker.

structure.explanation: In a longer conversation, combine patterns instead of translating word-for-word: suggest a plan, give a reason, check that it suits the other person, then confirm. Repeated vocabulary from earlier lessons is deliberately not repeated as new vocabulary.
structure.exampleEn: Let’s meet tomorrow if that suits you.

notes.title: Propose
notes.detail: خلنا نرتب = Let’s organise.

notes.title: Make it considerate
notes.detail: Add this to show that the other person’s schedule matters.

notes.title: Confirm
notes.detail: Use a short confirmation to close the plan naturally.

exercises.question: إذا يناسبك softens a plan by meaning…
exercises.feedback: إذا يناسبك means “if it suits you”.

exercises.question: Which phrase can close and confirm a plan?
exercises.feedback: تمام، اتفقنا means “Great, agreed.”
